flags.observation: Opener plus card line reaches 106 characters; beats 10, 13, 18, 24, 26, 29, 33 also exceed 100, not one breath.
"backed by your grandparents’ promises" shifts the card's claim about who pays the money back.
"In English: a lion." plays as a riddle; the bridge from the previous card is unclear on first listen.
Line loses the bankers creating the loan out of nowhere; "war debts, and a private bank" blurs the causal claim.
"Grab a board" leaves the board image unanchored; the listener cannot tell which board is meant.
"Conductor? A clown." is the third question-and-snap opener; with beats 29 and 31 the cadence turns formulaic.
"money" appears three times in frame and opener text (beats 1, 3, 24), over the limit of two.
The card's claim concerns the Federal Reserve Act; the line never names it, so normies miss which act.
The card's lead claim, notes backed by future taxation, is dropped; only the gamble half survives.
Outro beat runs 132 characters in three clauses; the punch is hard to land as one quotable breath.
"The Fed's printer" sits uneasily beside beat 30's "isn’t printed"; the punch slightly contradicts the deck's own claim.
